newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish security spends on gadgets to protect Pope.
newsitem.headline: Polish security spends on gadgets to protect Pope.

text.p: Sophisticated equipment that stop bombs being detonated remotely or test food instantly for safety are on a $3 million shopping list drawn up by Polish security services for the coming visit of Pope John Paul.

Interior Minister Leszek Miller said the government had allocated an extra 10 million zlotys ($3.2 million), above security services budgets, largely for equipment to be used when the Pope tours his native Poland from May 31 to June 10.

"Some is for revealing metal objects, or generators of so-called white noise -- these are special electromagnetic waves which prevent the remote detonation of explosive devices," Miller told public radio on Tuesday.

"There are many other such mechanisms such as those which can instantly assess the quality of food which will be served to our guests. This is very expensive equipment and hence the high costs," Miller said.
Miroslaw Gawor, head of the Government Protection Office (BOR), told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily in an interview that the Pope's food would receive special attention.
"Every meal will be checked by a doctor and an explosives expert," General Gawor said.
He also said his forces would check every flat with windows facing the route of the papal trip through 11 towns and cities and that they were already warning residents not to invite strangers.
Border guards and security services were also ensuring that "no unwanted people, such as Moslem fundamentalists, could come in from abroad," he said.
